figures.title: System architecture
figures.caption: Four-layer architecture of the current repository. LIFF REST traffic reaches Express directly; LINE mediates identity and chat. Tesseract runs locally in the app container. Gemini is optional and consent-gated. GitHub Actions runs the separate deadline evaluator.

figures.title: Core entity-relationship diagram
figures.caption: Core ERD showing seven domain tables, their fields and eight core foreign keys. Child-to-parent FK arrows carry parent/child multiplicities; composite score and attendance keys enforce matching sections. Creator attribution is detailed in Figure 3.

figures.title: Supporting entity-relationship diagram
figures.caption: Supporting ERD adds five tables and the seven remaining foreign keys, using students and sections as reference anchors. Together Figures 2 and 3 cover 12 physical tables, 89 columns and 15 foreign keys. Private records cascade; shared creator/actor attribution becomes null.

figures.title: Level-0 DFD / Context Diagram of Rord-Mai
figures.caption: Level-0 context DFD in the reference monochrome style. Student, LINE and Gemini exchanges are balanced against Level 1. The context contains one system process and no internal store.

figures.title: Level-1 DFD of Rord-Mai
figures.caption: Level-1 DFD in monochrome Gane-Sarson notation. Eight main processes exchange data with repeated aliases of Student, LINE, Gemini and the application database. D1 includes the domain tables, not a new physical table. Selected processes 2.0, 4.0 and 8.0 are expanded at Level 2.

figures.title: System workflow
figures.caption: Student workflow from LINE authentication through independent consent, shared section setup, private entry and comparison. OCR drafts require review. Norm-referenced grade estimates and repeated-course GPAX are explicitly restricted; failures preserve a manual or template path.

figures.title: Consent and data lifecycle
figures.caption: Consent lifecycle of the current implementation. Storage grant and optional external explanation consent are separate operations. External withdrawal preserves academic data; confirmed storage withdrawal or deletion removes private records and clears shared attribution. Provider records are outside database cascade scope.

figures.title: LINE intake and deadline delivery
figures.caption: Two independent LINE processing flows. Signed consented webhook work commits before acknowledgement; a consentless reminder stays request-local and sends afterward. A separate GitHub Actions runner rechecks eligible academic targets and consent, persists retry keys before sending, and records outcomes.

figures.title: Level-2 DFD for Process 2.0: Manage Consent
figures.caption: Level-2 decomposition of consent and confirmed private deletion. Child interfaces preserve the Student consent request/status and D1 account query, snapshot and update flows of parent 2.0. Deletion is rooted at students; database cascades remove private records and clear shared attribution.

figures.title: Level-2 DFD for Process 4.0: Calculate Results
figures.caption: Level-2 calculation decomposition. Owned inputs produce weighted summaries, required target scores, and permitted ordinary stay/withdraw GPAX scenarios. Repeated-course GPAX emits REPEAT_RULE_UNVERIFIED rather than fabricated replacement arithmetic. Child boundary flows match process 4.0.

figures.title: Level-2 DFD for Process 8.0: Deadline Notifications
figures.caption: Level-2 notification decomposition. Current course, consent and delivery data produce eligible persisted notifications, a bounded LINE push and delivery-state updates. Existing retry keys are reused; no second notification is created for the same student/section. Interfaces balance with process 8.0.
